questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Continuous Integration”?
options: Continuous Integration should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Continuous Integration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Continuous Integration means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Continuous Integration removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Continuous Integration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Continuous Integration is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Automated builds” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Automated builds” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Automated builds” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Automated builds” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Automated builds” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Automated builds” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Automated builds” under Continuous Integration. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Continuous Integration”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
